_source: Transcribed from the Claude Design handoff bundle's DISTRICTS/GROUPS constants in Curia.dc.html (fetched 2026-07-30). lat/lon/base/r/span are the prototype's own map-projection values, kept as-is so the real map behaviour can be ported rather than re-derived.
_accentColorSource: The five Cheshire districts' original accentColor values (transcribed from the prototype, per CLAUDE.md's Design tokens table) all sat in a narrow gold/tan/olive hue range — technically distinct hex values, but not perceptually distinct once rendered as the real map's low-opacity blurred glow (2026-08 user report, testing from Wilmslow: 'the districts are all glowing the same colour'). Widened the hue spread for these five specifically (gold → amber → terracotta → rust-brown → olive) while staying inside the closed warm palette CLAUDE.md's Design tokens section governs — per that section's own note, per-district accent colors are explicitly 'extensible... not a fixed set', unlike the core UI palette. Manchester's five (2026-08, same user, same complaint against a Manchester screenshot this time, with explicit requested hues: 'northern quarter is a purple, deansgate is an orange, spinningfields a soft blue') now deliberately step outside the warm-only cluster — purple/blue read as genuine outliers against CLAUDE.md's 'avoid bright primary colors' general aesthetic note, so both are kept desaturated/dark-mode-muted (plum and slate, not violet and cyan) rather than literal primaries, and are only 2 of the 5 so the family still reads warm overall. Ancoats and Chinatown weren't named by the user; picked a rust-brick and a crimson-berry respectively to keep real hue separation from Deansgate's orange and from each other. The user's own scoping note applies here too: colors only need to be distinct from what's actually visible together — Northern Quarter's purple can freely be reused by a far-off district (e.g. Hale) without conflict, since the two are never both zoomed-in at once.
_editorialDescriptionSource: Added by curia-moments-journeys (M6) for the district guide screen. Northern Quarter/Ancoats/Spinningfields/Deansgate are transcribed (Ancoats lightly trimmed to drop a specific venue count tied to the prototype's own DETAIL.v list, which doesn't match this file's seed venues) from the prototype's own DETAIL constant. Chinatown/Altrincham/Hale/Wilmslow/Alderley Edge/Mobberley have no DETAIL entry in the prototype (it falls back to a generic Cheshire blurb for any district without one) — their copy below is original, written to the Brand voice bar in CLAUDE.md, not transcribed.
_metroScopeNote: Los Angeles (Beverly Hills, West Hollywood, Santa Monica, Venice, Culver City) was added as a real metro in an earlier 2026-08 pass, then removed at explicit later request (2026-08) to keep the app scoped to Manchester/Cheshire only. This coincidentally restores CLAUDE.md's own 'Districts — resolved to the prototype's real 10, across two metros' section to being accurate again — it was already stale while LA existed, and was flagged as such but never updated in CLAUDE.md itself while that was true.

districts.name: Northern Quarter
districts.editorialDescription: Loudest of the ten, and honest about it. Best treated as a second or third stop rather than the whole evening — the good rooms are upstairs, behind doors with no signage.

districts.name: Ancoats
districts.editorialDescription: Mill brick and low ceilings, run by people who used to cook somewhere more famous and left on purpose. It peaks late and rewards walking — the best of it sits within a few minutes of the canal.

districts.name: Spinningfields
districts.editorialDescription: Glass, height and expense accounts. It empties by eleven on a weeknight, which is either the flaw or the appeal depending on the evening you had in mind.

districts.name: Deansgate
districts.editorialDescription: The formal spine of the city — hotel bars, height, and service that still wears a jacket. Reliable rather than surprising, which on a Tuesday is the point.

districts.name: Chinatown
districts.editorialDescription: Smaller than its name suggests, and better after dark than at lunch. A handful of rooms worth detouring for, tucked in behind the arch most people only photograph.

districts.name: Altrincham
districts.editorialDescription: A market town playing at being a city district, and mostly winning. Independent cinema, small plates, and a pizza queue nobody minds standing in.

districts.name: Hale
districts.editorialDescription: Village high street money — quieter than Altrincham, later than it looks from the outside. Best on a Friday, when the terrace tables fill before the sun goes.

districts.name: Wilmslow
districts.editorialDescription: The polished end of the Golden Triangle. Understated storefronts hiding rooms that assume you already know what you want.

districts.name: Alderley Edge
districts.editorialDescription: Sandstone and fireplaces, with the actual Edge — the wooded ridge, not a marketing name — a ten-minute walk from most of it. Earlier nights than the city, and no worse for it.

districts.name: Mobberley
districts.editorialDescription: The quiet edge of the set — fewer rooms, longer drives, and exactly the kind of evening that rewards both.

_dayMultiplierSource: The prototype's DAY_MULT table is global (not per-district) — applied identically to every district by src/lib/data/seed.ts. Keys are full lowercase day names to match src/lib/scoring/rank-venues.ts's resolveContext() day format.
_bandMultiplierSource: The prototype's BAND_MULT table, keyed by District.kind ('city' vs 'county') — the default every district falls back to. A district can still carry its own per-district `bandMultiplier` override directly on its entry instead (District.bandMultiplier in src/types/models.ts, preferred over the kind-based table by src/lib/data/seed.ts whenever present) when sharing the generic curve would flatten real differences in character — used for Beverly Hills/West Hollywood during the LA metro's lifetime (2026-08, at explicit user request: 'make districts feel alive... different districts... busy at different times'), removed along with the rest of that metro (see _metroScopeNote). No district currently uses an override, but the mechanism stays — a genuine judgment call grounded in real character, not transcribed from the prototype (no per-district curve exists there), worth keeping for whatever district needs it next.
